sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU with WebGL fallback, Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; WebRTC and BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded / ink look; warm paper, navy outlines, mint storefronts and coral accents
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks; original idle, run, jump, duck and celebration animations
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized ragtime music (10% default), procedural effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world cooperative sessions; standalone direct WebRTC co-op, same-browser BroadcastChannel rooms; 1–2 players including couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Real Rapier scripted three-case playthrough; headless Chromium WebGPU; emulated standard gamepad and multitouch; offline audio waveform checks; two-browser WebRTC and BroadcastChannel; official AI Hub standard, adverse-network, host-leave and dedicated-server harness. Visual art checked through WebGL because headless WebGPU screenshots can be blank. Physical controller and real mobile hardware: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No source research; native model knowledge. Supplied AI Hub integration instructions and client files read.

testingFeedback: 18 game/integration issues were found and fixed, along with 3 test-script issues and 1 headless-browser configuration issue.
3 were game breaking: dedicated-server input sequencing, the guest remaining blocked on a case report, and hidden server rendering delaying a session startup.
The real two-browser full-shift/restart regression verified authority, lift controls, guest case transitions and replay.
The first headless WebGPU screenshot was blank and could not establish whether the scene rendered. Device health and draw submissions were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js combines procedural geometry, TSL cel materials and native AnimationMixer clips well in a single-file game.
Yes. The supplied Chromium WebGPU flags lost even a one-cube device. Adding --use-angle=swiftshader and --disable-vulkan-surface fixed the test environment.
The three-floor chase simulation, transport interactions, controller interface and authoritative cooperative state synchronization.
Keeping physical floor travel, animated character poses and networked case transitions consistent, while validating headless WebGPU rendering.
A built-in toon node material with matching WebGPU and WebGL behavior.
promptFeedback: The specific arcade source, controller-first design and procedural audio requirements gave the game a clear identity.

The no-internet research rule overlaps with a linked integration contract that must be retrieved; I used native knowledge for the source and fetched only the required integration and runtime dependencies.
Combining a complete three-case game, generated art and audio, live developer tools and authoritative multiplayer in one HTML file.
Include versioned local AI Hub client/harness files and known-good headless browser flags.

aiHub.name: Keystone Bumbling Beat
aiHub.tagline: Catch the crook. Mind the merchandise.
aiHub.description: Clock in for three slapstick mall chases. Hop trolleys, duck toy planes, and take a lift to cut off a light-fingered rascal, solo or with a partner.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / A,D move; Cross / Space jump; Circle / Down duck; Triangle / E use shortcut; Square / Shift burst; Options / Esc pause.
